title: ACCY 6900 — Professionalism, Policy and Research

questions.prompt: SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin No. 99 addresses:
questions.explanation: SAB 99 is titled Materiality (August 12, 1999).

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: SAB 99’s core view is that exclusive reliance on certain quantitative benchmarks to assess materiality is:

choices.text: Inappropriate; misstatements are not immaterial simply because they fall beneath a numerical threshold

questions.explanation: Exclusive reliance on quantitative benchmarks is inappropriate.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: In SAB 99’s fact pattern, combined misstatements overstate net income by 4% and no line item is misstated by more than 5%. Management concludes the deviation is immaterial. The staff’s question is whether a registrant may assume immateriality below a percentage threshold. The interpretive response is:
questions.explanation: Interpretive Response: No.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: The staff has no objection to a 5% “rule of thumb” as:

choices.text: An initial step in assessing materiality

questions.explanation: A percentage threshold may provide a preliminary assumption; quantifying is only the beginning of the analysis.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: FASB Concepts Statement No. 2, as quoted in SAB 99, says an item is material if it is probable that the judgment of a reasonable person relying on the report would have been:

choices.text: Changed or influenced by inclusion or correction of the item

questions.explanation: Magnitude such that a reasonable person’s judgment would have been changed or influenced.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: The Supreme Court formulation quoted in SAB 99 is that a fact is material if there is a substantial likelihood a reasonable investor would view it as significantly altering the:
questions.explanation: TSC Industries formulation: total mix of information.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: SAB 99 says financial management and the auditor must consider both:
questions.explanation: Consider both “quantitative” and “qualitative” factors.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: The FASB rejected formulating general quantitative materiality standards because:

choices.text: Investors never care about small amounts
Materiality judgments can properly be made only by those who have all the facts

questions.explanation: No general standards of materiality could take into account all considerations in experienced human judgment.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: Which qualitative factor may render a quantitatively small misstatement material under SAB 99?

choices.text: Whether it masks a change in earnings or other trends
Whether the 10-K is filed on a Tuesday
Whether the auditor’s office has a window

questions.explanation: Among the listed considerations: masking a change in earnings or other trends.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: Changing a loss into income (or vice versa) is listed in SAB 99 as:

choices.text: A qualitative consideration that may make a small misstatement material

questions.explanation: Whether the misstatement changes a loss into income or vice versa.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: A misstatement that helps management meet a bonus target is:

choices.text: A qualitative factor that may make a small amount material

questions.explanation: Whether it increases management’s compensation, e.g., by satisfying bonus requirements.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: SAB 99 warns that even small intentional misstatements to “manage” earnings:
questions.explanation: Do not assume even small intentional misstatements, e.g. earnings management, are immaterial.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: When aggregating misstatements, SAB 99 says a material misstatement of an individual amount:

choices.text: Can be offset by an equal error in the opposite direction always
Cannot be eliminated by combining it with other misstatements

questions.explanation: If an individual amount causes the statements as a whole to be materially misstated, that effect cannot be eliminated by other misstatements.

questions.module: Illustrative Documents for Handout #3
questions.prompt: Registrants and auditors should consider each misstatement:

choices.text: Only if it exceeds 10% of assets
Only if the CEO requests it

questions.explanation: Consider each misstatement separately and the aggregate effect of all misstatements.
